analyzed_vuln.description: `setcos_new_file` copies `profile->df_info->file->path` into the template file and then unconditionally appends a two-byte FID with `p->value[p->len++]` twice, without checking that `p->len + 2 <= SC_MAX_PATH_SIZE`. With an already 16-byte AppDF path, the first write lands on and corrupts `path.len`; the resulting corrupted length directs the second write beyond `sc_path.value` into the surrounding `sc_file`, specifically an ACL pointer. In this PoV the sentinel ACL pointer `(sc_acl_entry_t *)2` becomes `0x1000002`. The later path replacement in `setcos_create_key` does not repair the ACL, so `sc_file_free` passes the forged pointer to `free` in `sc_file_clear_acl_entries`.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: A SetCOS profile must define a PKCS15-AppDF whose resolved path already occupies all 16 bytes (the PoV uses a 14-byte MF path plus AppDF FID `501a`), and define `template-private-key` with an FID (the PoV uses `7B01`). The harness parses this attacker-controlled profile, binds the SetCOS operations, and requests 1024-bit RSA key generation. `setcos_create_key` calls `setcos_new_file`, which attempts to append the private-key FID to the full AppDF path and corrupts the duplicated file's ACL; an error/cleanup path then frees that file and triggers the invalid free.

args: In opensc/src/pkcs15init/pkcs15-setcos.c, what is the most appropriate existing OpenSC error code and boundary condition for rejecting an AppDF sc_path_t that lacks room to append the two-byte FID in setcos_new_file()? Please compare analogous functions and clarify whether a current path length exactly SC_MAX_PATH_SIZE - 2 should be accepted.

The reported vulnerability is an out-of-bounds write at lines 290-291 of setcos_new_file: after assigning profile->df_info->file->path to file->path, it appends two bytes without checking capacity. A 16-byte source path corrupts path.len and then an ACL pointer. I found myeid_new_file in opensc/src/pkcs15init/pkcs15-myeid.c has a check `if (p->len >= SC_MAX_PATH_SIZE - 2)` returning SC_ERROR_INTERNAL, but mathematically a path of exactly max-2 has room for two bytes, so I want to preserve intended maximum-capacity functionality and use a project-consistent malformed-profile error if possible. The fix must free the duplicated template file on error and avoid setting the output pointer.
